FLE-001.title: The Fleeca Job

overview.target: Fleeca Bank — Great Ocean Highway Branch
overview.objective: Infiltrate Fleeca's security network, obtain access codes, and execute a coordinated robbery.

FLE-001.intel: Lester Crest begins assembling a professional crew capable of executing high-value criminal operations across Los Santos. The Fleeca Job serves as the first major heist operation, testing the crew's ability to perform reconnaissance, bypass security, coordinate transportation, and manage law enforcement response.

planningLocation.observation: Apartment Connection: 4 Integrity Way, Apartment 30. Visible Landmark: Fleeca Bank flags. Possible Connection: the apartment view appears to reference the first heist target.

setup.name: 1. Scope Out Fleeca Bank
setup.objective: Before committing to the job, the crew stakes out the target branch to map its security setup from the outside — camera coverage, guard rotations, exactly where the vault sits relative to the main floor, and the fastest route out once the alarm goes up.
setup.locations: Fleeca Bank — Great Ocean Highway branch
setup.intel: Scouting confirms camera placement, guard numbers on duty, the vault's position inside the building, and which street offers the cleanest getaway from the first wave of responding police.
setup.dialogue:
There's a Fleeca franchise on the Western Highway near Chumash. Take us there. Word of warning, we're on the job right now, so don't let the cops notice you. If they come after us, we call it off. So, my taciturn friends, I suppose you want to know how we're doing this. Well, funny you should ask. We're driving out to the bank, taking a look at it, Picking up some equipment, and then heading back to make our plans. Not very complex at all. We're not going in, we're not poking it with a stick, we're just sitting back and taking a look. You see, I like my scores like I like my dates – across the street and unaware they’re being watched.

Alright, so why this bank, over all the other banks in the state, why does fortune favour this one? Another good question. You're full of good questions. You're like a child whose parents think it's clever, or the IRS. Well, this bank’s got some safety deposit boxes, and in one of those boxes are some bonds being hidden from the tax man, that no one's going to report missing. All starting to make sense?

Security should be like, well, relatively light, if your day dreams are raids on the Union Depository. Quite heavy, if your day job is turning over liquor stores and gas stations. And the bonds in the box will be worth more than a few rumpled notes from the till, so, the minor escalation is worth it... if you can handle it. Plus, you know, the seaview. Nothing like staring at the ocean while you contemplate money and power and incarceration, and homicide, you know all those weighty issues in your first foray into serious armed robbery. I'm assuming you're a kind of cerebral crew, because otherwise, this whole not talking to you just kind of put you on the spectrum, right? Okay, well, how about we just get there and see where we're at. There it is. Take a look. Drink it in.

I've patched into the security feed on my cell. Take a look. What are we looking at? Small joint. Not much security. Staff won’t give a crap, especially about the deposit boxes. Customers will probably be thinking how to turn this into a screenplay. The boxes are in the back behind the safe door. We want box number 167. It's right on the highway with good access. That'll work for you, you can get out quick. But it'll also work for the cops, speeds up the response time. Okay? Okay.

Enough of this peeper crap. Let's go to the Garment Factory. Now, when you hit the bank, you're going to need to hack into its security system. I've written a neat little program that'll do most of the work for you, but it's probably a good idea to familiarize yourselves with it. You in the passenger seat, I’ve sent it to your phone (BitterSweet). Take it for a dry run, keep your hands steady, and maybe the wet run won't be a disaster.
I'm calling Paige. She's my assistant. First, she's going to get us what we need, and then she's going to saw me in half. Hahaha. No? Didn't like that one? Huh, you don't make it easy.

Paige, it's Lester... Place looked good. Nothing we weren't expecting… Can you get the Intel together? Hard copies to go on a notice board... Yeah. Plus all the equipment we spoke about. I'll be over to collect it with those people... Yeah...Mmm, charming as ever...Okay, see you soon. Hey passenger seat, get into their network? Good work.
She's loading the hardware into the back of a truck (Declasse Granger). Tools for the job, things for you to wear. On a job, your attire will depend on the role you're performing. As the jobs get more complicated, so will the uniforms. If you're likely to be seen by civilians, you'll be provided with a couple of masks, then, when you go into the bank, you can choose one that... goes with your eyes . And hey, there's the added bonus of none of your favourite comic convention outfits being linked to a major crime. Haha, whoop-dee-doo. Where were we? Masks! Paige! Oh yeah. We'll go over there, pick her up, and go back to your place to plan this thing. There's Paige. We're leaving this car, taking the truck. I should be using my cane.

Paige: 
Nice to meet you.

Lester:
Come on. Back to your place.

Lester: 
Is it all there?

Paige:
I think so... You wanna get out and check, go down the inventory? Or are you happy sitting there making a perfect butt imprint on your easy-wipe seat?

Lester:
I’ll take your word for it.

Paige:
Thank you. It should all be there. The clothes. Guns. Headsets, Masks, The Drill. The files with all the photos and surveillance work. Hey, there’s enough here to make us all look real suspicious. Nice little conspiracy to commit robbery charge waiting to happen.

Lester:
What, they gonna charge us with thought crime?

Paige:
Not so much thought as everything-but-the-deed-crime. We’d be caught with our pants down and a hard on out to here.

Lester:
Well, we’re not getting caught. These are professionals.

Paige:
So I hear. The cheapest professionals money can buy.

Lester:
I like to think of it as investing in new talent. She didn't mean anything by that, by the way. She’s just a little brusque.

If they were offended, they would’ve said something.

setup.name: 2. Kuruma
setup.objective: With the target scouted, the crew needs a vehicle tough enough to survive a running gunfight with law enforcement during the getaway. An armored Kuruma fits — unremarkable enough not to draw attention beforehand, but built to shrug off small-arms fire once things go loud.
setup.locations: Acquired ahead of time and stored for the final job
setup.intel: The armored Kuruma becomes the crew's default getaway vehicle for the operation, prioritizing survivability over raw speed.

roles.duties: Positions the armored Kuruma outside the bank and holds it there under fire while the Driller works, then pilots the getaway once the vault's open — threading through the responding police without losing the vehicle or the haul.

Goes in on foot to breach the safety deposit boxes. Vault security resets after a set window, so it's a race against time as much as a drilling job — speed matters as much as getting through the door cleanly.

PRI-002.title: The Prison Break

overview.objective: Break Professor Maxim Rashkovsky out of Bolingbroke Penitentiary and get him out of the country.

PRI-002.intel: Agent 14 outlines the setup jobs needed before the breakout: securing an aircraft for Rashkovsky's escape flight, hijacking a prison transport bus, obtaining the inmate transfer schedule, retrieving Rashkovsky's car from a rival theft ring, and cleaning up loose ends connected to his case.

DOOM-012.title: Act I — The Data Breaches

overview.target: Data on a series of breaches targeting sensitive government information
overview.objective: Investigate who's behind the breaches and feed the recovered data to Avon's AI, Clifford, for analysis.

DOOM-012.intel: Lester and tech billionaire Avon Hertz recruit the crew to track down a string of data breaches, framing it as a straightforward recovery job. Requires owning a Facility to unlock the planning room. Three prep missions (Paramedic Equipment, Deluxos, Akula) unlock three setup missions before the finale — this act is the gentlest introduction to the trilogy, but it's what puts the crew on Avon's radar for what's coming in Acts 2 and 3.

setup.name: Paramedic Equipment
setup.objective: Break into an ambulance depot and steal a set of paramedic equipment — jumpsuits, a defibrillator, and the rest of an EMT loadout — needed to convincingly pose as first responders at the courier's crime scene.
setup.intel: This is what makes the Dead Courier job work: showing up to a police-taped crime scene dressed as paramedics is the only way to get close to the body without setting off every cop in the area.
setup.dialogue:
“Sending you the location now. In case it wasn't clear, you're gonna need the ambulance and the paramedic gear to get into the Coroner's Office. You know, to get the agent's body, to get the data, yeah? Okay. Get to work.”
—Lester's briefing.

“You got it? Alright. Now bring it back to the facility in one piece and we'll call it a job well done.”
—After taking the Ambulance.

“Stealing data just doesn't have the same, uh... allure as analogue theft, am I right? I mean, it's just not sexy. But soon all money will be data and this will be the only gig going, so... there's that. We should just enjoy it while it lasts.”
—On the way to the Facility.

“Avon is exactly the kind of guy I'd like to rob... and I'm working for him. He better pay us so much, it's like we robbed him!”
—When closer to the Facility.

“Or, you could just call up an ambulance and get it to come to you, of course. I thought that was pretty obvious, so I didn't mention it. Now bring it back to the facility in one piece and we'll call it a job well done.”
—Shortly after calling 911.

“Good work getting that, um, "thing" for the, uhh... "job". Hey, um, you ever want to outsource that kind of work, there's always people who can get us things for a price. Yeah? Something to think about if your time is precious.”
—After delivering the Ambulance.

setup.name: Dead Courier
setup.objective: A government courier has turned up dead with a data cache still on them. The crew poses as first responders — stealing an ambulance is the cleanest way to reach the body without drawing attention — then recovers the cache before anyone else gets to it.
setup.intel: The cache turns out to be only half the puzzle — it points toward a wider signal network still broadcasting data the crew hasn't accounted for.

setup.name: Deluxos
setup.objective: Steal a prototype Deluxo — an amphibious, flight-capable sports car — from the guarded lab or warehouse it's being developed in, then deliver it back to the Facility.
setup.intel: The Deluxo is what makes Signal Intercepts possible — its flight mode is the only way to keep pace with intercept targets moving across both land and water.

setup.name: Signal Intercepts
setup.objective: Using the amphibious, flight-capable Deluxos acquired in prep, the crew tails a set of moving targets — armored vans first, then boats — getting close enough to hack each one with the SecuroServ app before it can relay its data onward.
setup.locations: Across land and waterways in Los Santos
setup.intel: Each hacked target has to be destroyed immediately after the hack completes, and every vehicle carries an armed passenger, so it's equal parts stealth-hacking and running gunfight.

setup.name: Akula
setup.objective: Steal an Akula stealth attack helicopter from a heavily guarded military installation and fly it back to the Facility undetected.
setup.intel: The Akula's stealth systems are what let the crew land undetected on the NOOSE facility roof for Server Farm — showing up in anything else gets the whole approach blown before it starts.

setup.name: Server Farm
setup.objective: With the Akula stealth helicopter from prep, the crew flies undetected onto the roof of a NOOSE facility, then moves in on foot to quietly clear guards and cameras on the way to the server room.
setup.intel: Once inside, the job becomes a stealth puzzle — four servers need hacking while staying out of guard sightlines, since running or getting spotted blows the whole approach.

roles.duties: Fights into the IAA facility itself to physically stop the ongoing server hack before it completes.
Provides outside cover and mans the war room's gun camera system to clear remaining resistance while the infiltration team works.

DOOM-013.title: Act II — The Bogdan Problem

overview.target: Bogdan — a rogue foreign agent operating an armed submarine off the San Andreas coast
overview.contact: Lester Crest / Avon Hertz / Agent ULP
overview.objective: Work with Agent ULP to track down and neutralize Bogdan before he can destabilize the region.

DOOM-013.intel: Escalates hard from Act 1 — what looked like a data recovery job turns into tracking down a genuine rogue agent with a submarine off the coast. Five prep missions (Keycards, ULP Intel, Riot Control Van, Acquiring Strombergs, Acquiring Torpedo ECUs) build toward four setups that gather the intelligence and hardware needed to actually find and hit Bogdan's sub.

setup.name: Key Cards
setup.objective: Track down and steal the keycards needed to access the facility where the Avenger is being held, clearing the way to acquire it.
setup.intel: Without these, the Avenger job doesn't happen — this is the access prep for the rest of Act 2's mobile command post.
setup.dialogue:
“There's a location up on your GPS. Now we need a NOOSE van, to get a keycard, to get in an aircraft hangar, to steal an Avenger. Because the Russians are here... on a submarine. Okay, you got that? Good. A NOOSE team's been called out to help the LSPD with some bank robbers, or something. So get their van while they're occupied and bring it to me. Remember when we just robbed banks, eh? What innocent times those were.”
—Lester's briefing.

“I feel like Mrs. Rackman is not a lady we wanna trifle with. Unless we wanna end up in a secret foreign prison that is. I mean, do you wanna end up at an IAA black site? Yeah, me neither.”
—Commenting about their alliance with the IAA.

“Look out, our bank robbers have made the oh-so-wise decision to shoot their way to glory through a gas station! It could go up at any time. But, I don't know, maybe that's what you want. Hard to know.”
—When approaching to the gas station.

“My my. You all alright, huh? The van's still intact, so, uhh... so get it back here!”
—When close to the van.

“I should probably say, we'd rather you didn't bring the cops here... we've, uhh, kinda got enough to deal with right now.”
—When taking the van.

“There's a sub off the coast. Foreign agents everywhere, and no real explanation of what's going on! I'm sure there are conspiracy videos about this online, but... I'm too scared to watch 'em.”
—When closer to the Facility.

“So, the setup jobs are a big deal ahead of the final operation, the move on the submarine. So we always gotta make sure we have the equipment we need. Might seem like this prep work is small fry, but details matter! We need this stuff, but it's not so important how we get it: source it, steal it from rival crews, throw money down to buy it, whatever. Get the equipment and we can do the job and we can get paid.”
—After delivering the Police Riot to the Facility.

setup.name: Avenger
setup.objective: Secure a Avenger jet, which becomes the crew's new mobile operations base for the rest of the act — replacing the Facility as the planning hub while at sea.
setup.intel: The Avenger's mobility is the whole point here — Bogdan's submarine moves, so the crew needs a base that can move with it.

setup.name: ULP Intel
setup.objective: Recover intel pinpointing Agent ULP's location before Bogdan's people find them first.
setup.intel: This is what turns Rescue ULP from a blind search into a targeted extraction.
setup.dialogue:
“Okay, so we're looking for the whereabouts of this missing IAA agent. ULP, they called him. He was last seen with some very bad people. Take out the targets sent to your phone, while I monitor various channels. ULP wasn't just heading up the investigation into these breaches... you know what else he was in charge of? The IAA's drug deals on the West Coast. They just can't help themselves... some of these bastards love selling rocks to fund their illegal wars.”
—Lester's briefing.

“At least there are some seemingly competent people at the IAA, like Mrs. Rackman. Though that Agent 14 had set the bar pretty low. Am I right?”
—Commenting about the IAA agents.

“Keep taking down those dealers, someone's gonna lead us to that missing agent!”
—After killing the first dealer.
“You take out enough of these criminals, they'll panic, and someone will start talking about the kidnapping.”
—After killing half of the dealers.

“Alright. We got it. One of his dealers set him up. I traced his cellphone to an apartment. Get over there, and recover anything that might tell us where they're holding him. And don't expect a friendly welcome.”
—After taking out all the dealers.

“Now look for a bag, Russian made, the cameras show him going in with it. Pick it up, and bring it in.”
—After taking out all the dealers inside the apartment.

“Any hope of finding that agent is in that bag. Bring it in for analysis, and uhh... watch out for any interested parties.”
—After retrieving the duffel bag from the apartment.

“Okay. This should lead us right to him. When you wanna put on a rescue, you know where to go.”
—After bringing the duffel bag to the Facility.

setup.name: Rescue ULP
setup.objective: Extract Agent ULP, the government asset who actually has intel on Bogdan's whereabouts and operations, before Bogdan's people can silence them.
setup.intel: ULP becomes the crew's inside source for the rest of Act 2 once safely extracted.

setup.name: Riot Control Van
setup.objective: Steal a riot control van, whose reinforced frame and crowd-control hardware make it the tool the crew needs to force their way into wherever the hard drives are being kept.
setup.intel: Sets up Salvage Hard Drives — the van does the heavy lifting getting the crew through whatever's standing between them and the data.
setup.dialogue:
“Get out to that spot. There are enemy agents all over the state, and we're trying to disrupt them however we can... which is why we need a riot control van. Which is why we need a riot. Which is why you're starting one... okay?”
—Lester's briefing.

“You might not have noticed this, but nice friendly corporations have bought up most of the public squares and parks in LS. Oh and they have their own nice friendly security guards to keep the peace. So get there and cause chaos, launch some tear gas, you know, punch a few folks. Just get in the mix, and wait for the riot van to arrive. Then steal it from the fascist pricks and come back. And don't kill anyone, it's just a riot, we don't want the cops there.”
—When approaching to the location.

“Okay, corporate HQ won't like the look of this. Keep it up!”
—When fighting with the rioters.

“Keep that fight going until the head office sends out the boys.”
—When progressing with the riot.

“This is a PR nightmare... the riot squad will be there soon.”
—When the riot is taking effect.

“Right on time, there's the RCV. Get it and bring it in!”
—When the riot squad is sent.

“Alright, this van might be the only thing that stands in the way of the Russians, or whoever they are, doing what they came here to do.”
—When taking the RCV.

“Is it weird that there's a Russian nuclear sub of the coast of San Andreas, or is that like par for the course? I'm not sure which answer to that question would be more disquietening.”
—Commenting about the presence of the submarine.

“A Russian invasion of Los Santos is definitely not something you would have expected a few years ago, but now I'm like... meh.”
—When approaching to the Facility.

“We got it. Okay, hit the Planning Room when you wanna try and stop these enemy agents.”
—After delivering the RCV to the Facility.

setup.name: Salvage Hard Drives
setup.objective: Recover hard drives holding further detail on Bogdan's submarine and operation, filling in the gaps ULP's intel alone can't cover.

setup.name: Strombergs
setup.objective: Steal a pair of Strombergs — missile-firing amphibious sports cars — needed to operate underwater and hold their own against Bogdan's defenses during recon.
setup.intel: One of two preps feeding into Submarine Recon; the Stromberg is what lets the crew actually get close to the sub without just the Kosatka for cover.
setup.dialogue:
“Okay, head out. The wrecked cars are on the back of repo trucks. This is for our reconnaissance on the Russian submarine just off the coast. If we wanna turn Ocelot Strombergs into assault vessels, we're gonna need Ocelot Strombergs. So bring the trucks they're being carried on into base, we'll repair the Strombergs, you know, make some adjustments and you'll be ready to go.”
—Lester's briefing.

“Okay, head out. Luckily, a rival Import/Export crew's done most of our work for us. They've got the wrecked cars on the back of some Wastelanders. I'll send you an image of what you're looking for.”
—Lester's alternate briefing.

“We have a Stromberg! Get the truck off those assholes, and bring it in.”
—When approaching to a valid target truck.

“That's what we're after. Repo the repo truck, and bring it in.”
—When approaching to a valid target truck.

“You found one! Now steal the truck and get it back to the facility.”
—When approaching to a valid target truck.

“That's one. Bring the whole truck in to the base.”
—When approaching to a valid target truck.

“No dice. Keep looking for a Stromberg.”
—When approaching to an invalid target truck.

“That's not what we're looking for.”
—When approaching to an invalid target truck.

“Strombergs are all that will work for this, I'm afraid.”
—When approaching to an invalid target truck.
When delivering the trucks

“Okay, we've got something to work with.”
—When delivering the first truck to the Facility.

“Well done, that's two of them.”
—When delivering the second truck to the Facility.

“Alright. Only looking for one more of these.”
—When delivering the third truck to the Facility.

“Okay, that's the set. We'll start working on the cars. When you've got the weapons system, we can move on the sub.”
—When delivering the last truck to the Facility.

setup.name: Torpedo ECU
setup.objective: Steal the torpedo ECU needed to arm the crew's hardware with functioning torpedoes ahead of the sub recon and the finale assault to come.
setup.intel: The second of the two preps feeding into Submarine Recon, alongside the Strombergs.
setup.dialogue:
“Head out to that point. If you're going underwater to look at that big bad Russian submarine, you'll need to protect yourselves... with torpedoes. That's easy enough, but... torpedoes need ECUs, which you can't get in this country. Luckily there are some arms dealers on a platform just over the maritime boundary, who uhh... might have some in stock... so go do your, uhh... duty free shopping.”
—Lester's briefing.

“When I said shopping, by the way, I meant stealing. Take control of the platform, and get the ECUs.”
—When approaching to the designated location.

“Okay, you got 'em. Use whatever you need on that platform, and bring it in!”
—When taking the ECUs.

“Considering that went down in international waters, it was barely even a crime... who am I kidding, of course it was. We're horrible! But we're trying to save America, so...”
—When leaving the barge.

“Mrs. Rackman holds the purse strings now. At the end of the day, she's the one we gotta please... Let's all play nice, and get our pay checks.”
—On the way to the Facility.

“Okay, okay, your ECUs are going in the torpedoes, your cars are repaired. We're ready for the move on the submarine whenever you are. Just go to Planning.”
—After delivering the Torpedo ECUs to the Facility.

“Well, your ECUs are going in the torpedoes, now you need something to fire them from. Get hold of some Strombergs, and we'll get you ready for the move on the submarine.”
—Alternative dialogue if Heist Prep: Strombergs is not complete.

setup.objective: Scout Bogdan's submarine directly ahead of the finale, confirming its position, defenses, and the safest approach vector.
setup.locations: At sea, off the San Andreas coast
setup.intel: This is the last piece before the finale — everything from the previous three setups feeds into planning the actual assault.

roles.duties: Handles aerial support during the assault, keeping Bogdan's defenses occupied from above while the submarine team moves in.
Infiltrates the submarine directly to track down and neutralize Bogdan at the source.

DOOM-014.title: Act III — The Doomsday Scenario

overview.objective: Stop Avon Hertz and his AI Clifford from executing a plan to trigger a global cataclysm.

DOOM-014.intel: The trilogy's turn: Avon Hertz — the billionaire who framed Acts 1 and 2 as a hunt for someone else's conspiracy — is revealed as the actual architect, with his AI Clifford as the instrument. Six prep missions (Marked Cash, Recon, Chernobog, Flight Path, Test Site Intel, Onboard Computer) build toward five setups that arm the crew for a direct assault on Avon's fortified base.

setup.name: Marked Cash
setup.objective: Steal a duffel bag of marked bills from a dead drop that the FIB has under surveillance.
setup.intel: One of two preps feeding into Rescue Agent 14, alongside Recon.

setup.name: Recon
setup.objective: Scout the location Agent 14 is being held, confirming guard patterns and the safest way in before committing to the extraction.
setup.intel: The second prep feeding into Rescue Agent 14, alongside Marked Cash.

setup.name: Rescue Agent 14

setup.name: Chernobog
setup.objective: Steal a Chernobog ballistic missile launcher away from Merryweather Security.
setup.intel: Sets up Escort ULP — the Chernobog's firepower is what actually keeps ULP alive on the route out.

setup.name: Escort ULP
setup.objective: Escort ULP safely clear of danger, using the Chernobog mobile anti-air platform secured in prep to cover the route.

setup.name: Flight Path
setup.objective: Take out an arms dealer to recover information on the Barrage ATV that's being flown into Los Santos.
setup.intel: Feeds directly into Barrage, tracking the ATV shipment the crew needs to intercept.

setup.name: Barrage
setup.objective: Push back an assault against the crew's own operations, buying time to keep preparing for the base itself.

setup.objective: Retrieve the Khanjali tank's test site location from the home of one of Avon's employees.
setup.intel: Sets up Khanjali — without this, the crew would be going into the test site blind.

CAS-016.title: Casino Story Missions

overview.objective: Get up to speed on the newly opened casino and its ownership before the real operation — the Diamond Casino Heist — becomes available.

CAS-016.intel: A short run of introductory missions that come with the casino's opening. They establish the Cheng family's ownership of the building, put the crew on their payroll doing odd jobs around the resort, and — critically — introduce the Arcade property as the base needed to unlock and plan the Diamond Casino Heist itself. Nothing here is a heist in its own right; it's the on-ramp to Phase 10's real centerpiece.

CAS-017.title: Diamond Casino Heist

overview.target: The Diamond Casino & Resort's vault — contents rotate between cash, art, gold, or diamonds
overview.objective: Plan from a player-owned Arcade, then commit to one of three finale approaches — Silent & Sneaky, The Big Con, or Aggressive — to breach the vault and get out with the loot.

CAS-017.intel: This is the first heist built around genuine player choice in approach rather than one fixed finale. Vault Keycards is the one shared general prep that's mandatory on every run regardless of approach; the rest of the shared preps (Patrol Routes, Duggan Shipments, Security Intel, Power Drills) are optional but repeated across all three approach cards since they apply no matter which one gets picked. The same approach can't be picked twice in a row, so the crew has to alternate.

setup.name: Vault Contents
setup.objective: Covers the scoping stage that applies before any approach gets picked — casing the resort and scouting the vault itself. Mandatory items unlock the prep board; optional ones make the finale itself easier or add extra flair.

operations.name: Scope Out Casino
operations.objective: Photograph every access point around the resort — staff lobby, waste disposal, roof terrace, helipad, and the security tunnel. Unlocks entry-point choice on the prep board.

operations.name: Scope Out Vault Contents
operations.objective: Scout the vault itself to identify what's actually stored there this run — cash, art, gold, or diamonds — since the reward rotates and isn't known ahead of time.
operations.intel: Diamonds pay out the highest but are also the rarest find; cash tends to come up most often.

operations.name: Select Approach
operations.objective: Commit to one of the three finale approaches — Silent & Sneaky, The Big Con, or Aggressive. The same approach can't be picked twice in a row.

operations.name: Scope All P.O.I.
operations.objective: Photograph every point of interest inside the casino, beyond just the entry access points.

operations.name: Scope All Access Points
operations.objective: Photograph every possible access point rather than just the ones needed for the chosen approach, for full flexibility on future runs.

operations.name: Purchase Casino Model
operations.objective: Buy a physical model of the casino for the Arcade planning room.
operations.intel: Cosmetic/planning-room extra, not required to run the heist.

operations.name: Purchase Security Legend
operations.objective: Buy a security legend/key overlay for the planning room.
operations.intel: Cosmetic/planning-room extra, not required to run the heist.

operations.intel: Cosmetic/planning-room extra, not required to run the heist.

setup.name: Silent & Sneaky
setup.objective: Build out a stealth-first loadout — the least prep-heavy of the three approaches on paper, but the least forgiving once inside. Rewards patience: staying fully undetected buys extra time inside the vault, which usually means walking out with the highest-value loot.

operations.name: Vault Contents
operations.objective: Shared scoping stage that applies before any approach or arcade choice — casing the resort and scouting the vault itself. This isn't tied to any single Arcade; it's the mandatory prep every run needs regardless of which of the six Arcades the crew is operating out of.

operations.name: Support Crew Selection

operations.name: Unmarked Weapons
operations.objective: Acquire untraceable weapons for the crew ahead of the finale.

options.name: Gang Cache
options.notes: Assault a Lost MC clubhouse in Paleto Bay or a Vagos clubhouse in La Mesa, fight through to the back, and haul out two duffel bags of weapons one at a time before the gang gives chase on the way out.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lost MC clubhouse (Paleto Bay) or Vagos clubhouse (La Mesa)

details.label: Pursuers
details.value: Gang members, Vagos give chase in Slamvans

options.name: Merryweather Weapons
options.notes: Kill Merryweather personnel at a compound to find a flight schedule, then chase down the Titan cargo plane it points to, blow open its rear door mid-flight, and grab the crates that fall out.

details.label: Location
details.value: Los Santos Naval Port, Sandy Shores Airfield, or Palmer-Taylor Power Station

details.label: Pursuers
details.value: Two waves of Buzzard Attack Choppers

options.name: Military Weapons
options.notes: Steal a Barrage ATV loaded with unmarked weapons straight out of Fort Zancudo's munitions depot, then lose a four-star wanted level before delivering it.

options.name: NOOSE Van
options.notes: Track down four NOOSE vans scattered around the map, blow their rear doors to check the contents, then steal the one actually carrying the weapons and lose a three-star wanted level.

details.label: Location
details.value: Four possible NOOSE van locations around Los Santos

options.name: Police Seizure
options.notes: Race the cops to a weapons cache before they seize it, sneaking around patrols at Stoner Cement Works to grab two sets of unmarked weapons.

options.name: Smugglers
options.notes: Hunt down a group of smugglers along the coast at Palomino Highlands, kill them for the location of a Tula seaplane loaded with weapons, then fly it to Sandy Shores Airfield.

details.label: Location
details.value: Palomino Highlands, deliver to Sandy Shores Airfield

operations.name: Getaway Vehicles
operations.objective: Secure the getaway vehicles used once the crew is clear of the casino.

options.name: Drag Race
options.notes: Interrupt an illegal drag race at LSIA or Sandy Shores Airfield and either chase down the racers or wait for them to loop back to the start, then take the getaway vehicles.

options.name: Illicit Importers
options.notes: Raid a semi-random smuggler unloading site (Rancho, Elysian Island, or Paleto Bay) and take out the crew before driving the getaway vehicles out, with the smugglers giving chase in Schafters.

details.label: Location
details.value: Little Bighorn Ave (Rancho), Chupacabra St (Elysian Island), or behind Clucking Bell Farms (Paleto Bay)

options.name: Lost MC
options.notes: Only comes up if Zach Nelson is the driver. Shoot open the rear doors of Benson trucks at a Lost MC hideout to find the stolen getaway bikes.

details.label: Location
details.value: Paleto Bay or Seaview Road, Grapeseed

options.name: Merryweather Shipment
options.notes: Only comes up if Chester McCoy is the driver. One vehicle is in a Merryweather convoy in transit, the other is guarded inside a cargo plane at an airfield — take both however you like.

details.label: Location
details.value: Convoy in transit, plus LSIA or Sandy Shores Airfield

options.name: Police Compound
options.notes: Sneak into a police impound warehouse (La Mesa or Rockford Hills), dodge patrolling officers, shift blocking vehicles out of the way, and drive the getaway vehicles out clean.

details.label: Location
details.value: La Mesa or Rockford Hills police station

options.name: Test Site
options.notes: Only comes up if Chester McCoy is the driver. Fight through Merryweather operatives and Insurgent Pick-Ups guarding a testing site, then outrun pursuing helicopters on the drive back.

details.label: Location
details.value: Merryweather test site on Elysian Island or Joshua Road

options.name: Valet Service
options.notes: Knock out the real valets at a hotel, put on their uniform, and wait at the entrance for the getaway vehicles to pull up — let the actual driver walk away before taking them.

details.label: Location
details.value: Opium Nights (LSIA) or Banner Hotel & Spa (Del Perro)

operations.name: Hacking Device
operations.objective: Retrieve a piece of NOOSE or FIB tech needed by the crew's Hacker to work the vault door during the finale.

operations.name: Bugstars Gear - Part 1
operations.objective: First half of the job to unlock the Bugstars maintenance/delivery disguise, this route's entry method.

operations.name: Bugstars Gear - Part 2
operations.objective: Second half of the Bugstars disguise job, completed straight after Part 1.

operations.name: Vault Drills
operations.objective: Acquire the drills needed to physically breach the vault door once inside, since the Big Con relies on drilling through rather than hacking or blowing it open.

operations.name: Yung Ancestor: Dead Weight
operations.objective: Only unlocks if the roof terrace access point was photographed during Casino Scoping — Yung Ancestor asks the crew to get rid of a rental Fugitive for him, no questions asked.
operations.locations: Land Act Reservoir, then an abandoned lot in El Burro Heights
operations.intel: First part of a two-mission chain unlocking Yung Ancestor as a third possible entry disguise.
operations.dialogue: I swear, if that chopper come by again, I'm going to shove a rocket so far up its... Hey, is it done? Okay. Cool, cool. I owe you for that. Whole thing's got me so amped up.

operations.name: Yung Ancestor: After Party
operations.objective: Second half of the Yung Ancestor chain — paparazzi have photos of whatever Yung got up to at his penthouse party, and he wants them gone.
operations.intel: Take out four labeled paparazzi targets and destroy their cameras.

operations.name: NOOSE Gear
operations.objective: Secure a second disguise, worn as N.O.O.S.E. personnel, to swap into partway through the escape and slip past the police response that's already converged on the casino.

operations.name: Vault Key Cards
operations.objective: Acquire two keycards needed to access the mantrap between the casino floor and the vault itself. Mandatory on every approach.

operations.name: Patrol Routes
operations.objective: Photograph the guards' staff roster at a Duggan security meeting to learn exactly where every guard will be positioned during the heist.

operations.name: Duggan Shipments
operations.objective: Destroy weapons and equipment shipments meant for the casino's Duggan-contracted security team. Ten targets exist around the map.

operations.name: Security Intel
operations.objective: Meet Vincent at Rockford Plaza after retrieving a stolen Gauntlet Hellfire, in exchange for a USB drive loaded with casino security information.

operations.name: Power Drills
operations.objective: A shared general prep item that carries over regardless of approach.

setup.name: Big Con - Maintenance
setup.objective: The Big Con approach using the Bugstars maintenance-crew disguise as the entry method, plus the Yung Ancestor side chain that unlocks a second disguise option within this same route.

operations.name: Vault Contents
operations.objective: Shared scoping stage that applies before any approach or arcade choice — casing the resort and scouting the vault itself. This isn't tied to any single Arcade; it's the mandatory prep every run needs regardless of which of the six Arcades the crew is operating out of.

CAY-019.title: Cayo Perico Heist
CAY-019.type: Kosatka-based heist, 1-4 players, first fully solo-capable heist

overview.target: Juan "El Rubio" Strickler's private island compound
overview.objective: Infiltrate El Rubio's island, steal a primary target plus optional secondary loot, and escape.

CAY-019.intel: The first GTA Online heist completable entirely solo. Planned from a player-owned Kosatka submarine, whose owner Pavel runs the whole operation. Unlike every earlier heist, preps aren't a one-time unlock — they get destroyed and have to be redone before every single run, since (per Pavel) leaving equipment behind risks El Rubio tracing it back to the crew. Preps fall into four categories: Approach Vehicle, Equipment, and Weapon Loadout (all mandatory to unlock the finale) and Disruption (entirely optional, but makes the finale easier).

planningLocation.observation: El Rubio's island has an extensive sonar network — approaching by submarine requires stealing a sonar jammer from a Merryweather sub first.

setup.name: Gather Intel
setup.objective: Reach the island's Communications Tower, hack the switchbox, and locate the primary target to reveal loot values and routes. Cayo Perico has 8 infiltration points, 4 escape points, and 6 compound entry points in total — the first playthrough marks some as mandatory to find, but every site only needs discovering once and is remembered for future runs.

setup.name: Approach Vehicle
setup.objective: Choose how the crew actually reaches the island. The Kosatka's own approach is mandatory as a fallback; the other five are optional and unlock different infiltration routes and entry points once completed.

operations.name: Kosatka (submarine approach)
operations.objective: Steal a sonar jammer from a Merryweather submarine at a test site, then use scuba gear to swim in undetected from the sub itself.
operations.intel: This is the baseline approach every player starts with, and unlocks the Drainage Tunnel infiltration point specifically.

operations.name: Patrol Boat
operations.objective: Steal a Kurtz 31 Patrol Boat and deliver it to a drop-off. Comes armed, so the crew has weapons to fall back on if things go loud, at the cost of being one of the slower approach options.
operations.intel: Unlocks West Beach, Main Dock, and North Dock as infiltration points.

operations.name: Longfin
operations.objective: Steal a Longfin off a trailer from a police station parking lot using a truck cab, then lose the cops before delivering it to the docks.
operations.intel: Lets the crew pose as drug smugglers for dock access; unlocks Main Dock and North Dock.

operations.name: Velum (airstrip approach)
operations.objective: Secure a Velum 5-Seater smuggler plane.
operations.intel: Unlocks the Airstrip infiltration point.

operations.name: RO-86 Alkonost (HALO jump)
operations.objective: Secure an Alkonost for a high-altitude jump onto the island.
operations.intel: Unlocks the HALO Jump infiltration point — fast, but leaves the crew with no way to bring loot out by air unless air defenses are separately disabled.

operations.name: Annihilator Stealth (helicopter drop)
operations.objective: Steal a Buckingham Annihilator Stealth and complete the Pilot prep alongside it.
operations.intel: Unlocks the North Drop Zone and South Drop Zone infiltration points — requires one of these two zones to already be scoped during Gather Intel.

setup.name: Equipment
setup.objective: Gear needed to actually get through the compound once on the island. Which pieces are mandatory depends on the primary target and chosen compound entry point — the Cutting Torch is a genuine optional alternative rather than a strict requirement.

operations.name: Demolition Charges
operations.objective: Search the Grapeseed Train Depot and the O'Neil Brothers' ranch for demolition charges, fighting off O'Neil Brothers along the way.
operations.locations: Grapeseed Train Depot, O'Neil Brothers Ranch

operations.name: Fingerprint Cloner
operations.objective: Acquire a fingerprint cloner needed to access certain locked compound doors without triggering an alarm.

operations.name: Safe Code
operations.objective: Only needed if the primary target turns out to be in the compound safe — collect the code from El Rubio's head of security at a party in his Diamond Casino penthouse.
operations.intel: Conditionally mandatory: skip it entirely if the primary target isn't in the safe this run.

operations.name: Cutting Torch
operations.objective: Search random toolboxes around a delivery location for a blue cutting torch, then deliver it to the Kosatka.
operations.intel: A genuine alternative for the Drainage Tunnel entry rather than a strict requirement — locations of the toolboxes are randomized each time.

setup.name: Weapon Loadout
setup.objective: Choose and acquire a weapon loadout for the finale itself. Mandatory to unlock the finale, though the exact loadout options are down to player preference rather than fixed named missions.

setup.name: Disruption
setup.objective: Entirely optional missions that weaken El Rubio's defenses ahead of time rather than gate the finale itself. Worth doing for a harder run, safe to skip entirely for a fast one.

operations.name: Power Station
operations.objective: Sabotage the island's power station ahead of the finale.
operations.intel: Disables security cameras and lighting, and reduces guards' vision range at night during the finale.

roles.duties: Enters the compound, reaches the underground vault, and steals the primary target plus any secondary loot. Solo-viable — the only heist finale in the game that is.
Covers the infiltrator and helps carry additional loot before the escape. Unlike every earlier heist, support crew here are paid a flat upfront fee rather than taking a cut of the payout.
$25,000 for on-call sniper support once air defenses are disabled. No guaranteed hit rate, and can actually raise the alarm on an otherwise-clean stealth run if he misses.
Throw a flare to call in a bombing run on a marked location — good for clearing a cluster of guards at range, can't be used inside the compound itself.
Provides aerial recon of guard positions without needing to scout the area on foot.

BDB-025.title: Bail Enforcement

overview.target: Standard and Most Wanted bail jumpers across Southern San Andreas
overview.contact: Maude Eccles and her daughter Jenette Eccles
overview.objective: Buy a Bail Office from Maze Bank Foreclosures, then run down bounties for Jenette using the office's Bail Enforcement System computer.

BDB-025.intel: Maude Eccles — the bounty hunter who helped break Michael, Franklin, and Trevor out of trouble back in the story mode — calls the player to kick this off. After buying any office, an intro cutscene introduces Jenette, who's running day-to-day operations. The office computer lists three Standard targets (refreshing hourly, 48-minute cooldown after completing one, payout roughly $35,000–$40,000 each) and one Most Wanted target (once per day, six possible targets in rotation, payout up to around $129,000). Every target is worth significantly more brought in alive — killing one cuts the reward by around 75% — so non-lethal tools like the Stun Gun are worth keeping in the van.

setup.name: Paleto Bay
setup.objective: The budget option. Cheapest office by a wide margin, but it's out in the north of the map, away from most of the action — expect more travel time to reach targets.
setup.locations: Paleto Boulevard, Paleto Bay (behind Willie's Supermarket)
setup.intel: Base price $1,650,000. Fully upgraded, roughly $4,110,000 — the cheapest of all five even maxed out.

operations.name: Beau Duggan (Duggan Family)
operations.objective: Jumped bail during a grand larceny trial after running a fake bank scam that cleaned out a few dozen people's life savings.
operations.intel: Note: players pass the Lowdown 93.1 FM billboard in La Fuente Blanca en route — "down-low" is a play on the station name.
operations.dialogue: Alright, so Beau Duggan, charged with grand larceny. Last we heard he was runnin' things on the down-low. The paper trail led us to an old bar, but the place has been out of business these past years. Shady, I know. My bets are, that's where to look.

operations.name: Bill Duggan (Duggan Family)
operations.objective: Rolling in Duggan money but still committing insurance fraud — burned down an apartment he was renting, killing the tenant's dog in the process.
operations.intel: Note: UCLS Bookworms t-shirts are sold at the Pier, specifically at Suburban; players pass a Suburban store in Banham Canyon en route to Del Perro.
operations.dialogue: Alright there's a bar in town with fraudster Bill Duggan's name on the deed. Used to run a business out back. Was shut down years ago but, word is, there's still plenty of football around there, so colour me curious... If there's one thing I've learned about the Duggans... They swarm together like rats. If we're gonna find one, we're gonna find a whole pack of the bastards, so be careful.

operations.name: Hunter Duggan (Duggan Family)
operations.objective: A record covering assault, embezzlement, arson, manslaughter, animal cruelty, and indecent exposure.
operations.intel: Office assumed from family grouping alongside Beau and Bill Duggan — not explicitly stated in the source note the way theirs were.
operations.dialogue: So what've we got? Assault, embezzlement, arson... Well, if we're looking for Hunter Duggan, I've been told he still has keys to some old dive bar his family owned once upon a time. Sounds like a good place to lay low and keep business tickin' over.

operations.name: Ricky Ji (Bank Robbery)
operations.objective: A Khangpae/Korean Mob button man with a signature of knocking customers' teeth out during armed robberies.
operations.intel: Office not explicitly stated in the source — placed here based on the robbery's Paleto Bay location, so treat this one as a guess rather than confirmed.
operations.dialogue: So Ricky, he runs with the Korean mob. One of their button men. Not afraid to get his hands dirty. We're talkin' armed robbery with a liberal use of arms. According to my sources he's on the job so now's your chance to grab him.

operations.name: Serenity Pierce (Lost MC)
operations.objective: Kidnapping and assault charges against a member of a biker gang.
operations.intel: Note: players pass the La Fuente Blanca horse stables en route; there's an arm-wrestling table outside the clubhouse warehouse.
operations.dialogue: So I sent you Pierce's usual hangout. Now, we're only interested in her and her kidnappin' and assault charges, but I'd be surprised if she's alone here. It's a clubhouse... you know what clubhouses are? It's where biker gangs go to get high, throw darts, and break each other's arms.

operations.name: Grace Whitney (Most Wanted)
operations.objective: A CEO suspected of conspiracy to murder, who fakes her own death to dodge her bail jump.
operations.locations: El Burro Heights (St. Fiacre Hospital), then Maze Bank
operations.intel: Two-part mission: verify the body isn't really hers at the morgue, then track her to her art gallery once the ruse is confirmed.
operations.dialogue: OK, so if I'm a billionaire trying to start a new life, the first thing I'm gonna need is cash. Apparently, Whitney's super into art... Got 'er own collection! I say we head over to her gallery to start. I got a feelin' she'll sell all her bullshit in there first.

operations.name: Brock Thompson (Most Wanted)
operations.objective: A former heavyweight boxer turned bad-steroid dealer, whose last batch killed half the front line of the Pounders.
operations.intel: Uses signal jammers around the city to stay untraceable; destroying them ambushes his convoy before it reaches an armed drop-off.
operations.dialogue: Alright, so Brock Thompson was last seen moving some steroids through the city in a convoy. His MO is using these signal jammers all over the city that make it impossible to track his location, so I'm thinkin' we start with those. We could definitely use the element of surprise in this fight.

setup.name: Davis
setup.objective: A solid budget-to-mid option close to central Los Santos, on Carson Avenue next to Herr Kutz Barber.
setup.intel: Base price $2,000,000.

operations.name: Colby Wright (Prison Bus Escape)
operations.objective: A federal fugitive who broke out of a prison transport bus after shooting up a Cluckin' Bell over a wrong order.
operations.intel: Note: players pass a Cluckin' Bell in Chamberlain Hills and Weazel News en route.
operations.dialogue: My phone's been blowin' up with news of this guy. Colby Wright, now officially a federal fugitive. That means there's a federal manhunt underway! Broke outta the prison bus earlier today, right after chewing the faces off of everyone else on board.

operations.name: Jalen Kennedy (Street Thug)
operations.objective: Drug trafficking and murder charges; frequents the Vanilla Unicorn and has a reputation for bothering the dancers there.
operations.intel: Requires hacking a CCTV network via phone to locate. Note: players pass the Vanilla Unicorn en route.
operations.dialogue: So, Jaylen Kennedy? Now, he's trouble. Charged with drug traffickin' with a side of murder and jumped bail. Hard to track down when he covers the trails so well. Now listen, I say this very rarely... CCTV is gonna be your friend today. If you can hack the network, then you can locate the target.

operations.name: Xavier Fremond (Street Thug)
operations.objective: Wanted for multiple homicide with no known address on file.
operations.intel: Also requires a CCTV hack via phone to pin down. Note: the comms tower hacked in Sandy Shores is owned by Badger; Trevor uses a Badger phone.
operations.dialogue: I like to think I earned my keep with some thorough researchin'. But Xavier's really pissed me off. No family address, no place of residence. All I've found is his last location. Not much but, it's a start. Now remember, he's wanted for multiple homicide, amongst other things, so just, y'know, watch yourself.

operations.name: Sabrina Grey (Mansion)
operations.objective: A finance chief charged with embezzlement — specifically from a veterans' charity — and burying whistleblowers under her pool.
operations.intel: Note: players pass the Daily Globe building en route.
operations.dialogue: Okay, we got ourselves a fancy one. Sabrina Gray, big finance chief, charged with embezzlement, and burying whistle blowers under the pool. Head to her mansion and make sure she knows the consequences of jumping bail.

operations.name: Omar Garcia (Most Wanted)
operations.objective: A car-stealing street racer with multiple hit-and-runs, infamous for a viral police chase where he drove a stolen convertible through a casino.
operations.locations: Lifeinvader HQ, then an LS car meet
operations.intel: Requires hacking Lifeinvader's servers to read his DMs and locate him, then tracking him to a car meet.
operations.dialogue: Heya! So, Omar Garcia can't sit still for more than 5 minutes. The plan is to hack his Lifeinvader profile, so we can read his DMs and figure out where to catch him. Start heading over to their headquarters and I'll catch you up on the way.

setup.name: Del Perro
setup.objective: Sits on the western coast near the Vespucci Canals and beachfront — good pick for players who spend more time on that side of the city.
setup.locations: Red Desert Avenue, Del Perro (behind The Grain of Truth)
setup.intel: Base price $2,350,000. Fully upgraded, around $4,590,000.

operations.name: Tommy Lim (Bank Robbery)
operations.objective: A rising Khangpae hitman and bank robber, known for shooting at tellers who take too long.
operations.intel: Office inferred from how the source formats this entry ("Tommy Lim - Del Perro") — treat as reasonably confident but not stated as explicitly as others.
operations.dialogue: Okay, Tommy Lim is a known Khangpae member with burglary and paid murder charges. Recent addition, but quickly rising up the ranks. Word is, he's got a background of bank robbery, when he's not a hitman.

operations.name: Rylee Rose (Lost MC)
operations.objective: Three counts of robbery with aggravated assault, running a crew of men within a biker gang.
operations.intel: Note: players pass the Penal Colony in Burton en route.
operations.dialogue: Okay, okay, okay, Rylee Rose... three counts robbery with aggravated assault. You should see what she did to these clerks. She bosses 'round a bunch of leather-clad men, and not in a fun way.

operations.name: India Wood (Mansion)
operations.objective: A fraudster who took out credit lines in her housekeepers' names, and is suspected of killing her own mother to inherit the family mansion and fortune.
operations.intel: Note: players pass Mors Mutual Insurance en route.
operations.dialogue: Alright, listen... So our fraudster, India Wood, she's an infamous nepo baby who wasn't getting enough "nep" so she killed 'er momma. Inherited her mansion, as well as her fortune, for now. My bet is, she'll be holed up there.

operations.name: Chaz Lieberman (Most Wanted)
operations.objective: An embezzler who owns half the city, hiding from the Armenian mob after losing borrowed money betting on the Pounders.
operations.intel: Requires hacking cell towers to triangulate his location before the Armenian mob gets to him first. Note: Los Santos Pounders apparel is sold at Suburban.
operations.dialogue: Hey partner, today we're picking up Chaz Lieberman, the embezzler currently hidin' from loan sharks. We'll need to hack a few cell towers to figure out exactly where he's at. So our friend Chaz here dug himself into quite the shithole! Turns out, these aren't just regular loan sharks... It's the goddamn Armenian mob!

operations.name: Leroy O'Neill (Most Wanted)
operations.objective: An O'Neill family member seemingly taking the fall for a string of bounties that don't match his reputation as the least tough of the family.
operations.locations: Abandoned Motel, then the O'Neill Farm
operations.intel: Office not explicitly restated in the source for this entry — placed adjacent to Chaz Lieberman based on where it appears in the document, so treat as unconfirmed. Keys are found in the basement room with the deck of cards; the player never goes upstairs.
operations.dialogue: Hey I got the last location of the O'Neill target locked in. My theory is he's taking the fall for the rest of the family, which wouldn't exactly be a surprise... the O'Neills are as rotten as a meth head's nut sack. Of course they throw him under the bus!

setup.name: Mission Row
setup.objective: Central Los Santos, right by the LSPD's Mission Row Police Station and major freeways — one of the most commonly recommended picks since it clusters well with other Downtown-area businesses like an Auto Shop.
setup.intel: Base price $2,390,000.

operations.name: Cook Mckenzie (Prison Bus Escape)
operations.objective: Jumped a prison bus while awaiting trial, then stole a regular city bus.
operations.intel: Note: players pass a Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Stand en route.
operations.dialogue: Okay, I got the alert this mornin'. A goddamn real-life super max prison break! Okay... I've sent you Kenzie's last location, where he jumped the prison bus. We have to grab him before anyone else does!

operations.name: Lil Prince (Street Thug)
operations.objective: Distribution, burglary, assault, and first-degree murder charges — has slipped through the authorities' hands multiple times.
operations.intel: Requires hacking the CCTV network via phone to find him. Note: players pass Dashound on the way from Mission Row, and a Los Santos Transit bus stop in Paleto Bay.
operations.dialogue: Everyone knows Lil' Prince. And everybody's trying to get him for something... murder, double murder, triple murder, you name it. I've got his last location but other than that you're on your own. When I think of bail bond enforcement, I think of transferable skills. Y'know, like hackin' into the CCTV network to find your target.

operations.name: Brigitte Foster (Mansion)
operations.objective: Fraud and embezzlement, plus running over a receptionist with a Pegassi during a stunt against a business rival.
operations.intel: Note: players pass Luxury Autos in Rockford Hills en route.
operations.dialogue: So if you're going after Bridget Foster then you need to know there's two things she's famous for. One... her massive freaking mansion. Two, her massive freaking attitude. With charges of fraud, embezzlement, and runnin' over an assistant, she's gonna take some convincing...

setup.name: Downtown Vinewood
setup.objective: The premium option — most expensive of the five, but centrally placed with strong connectivity to both the northern rural areas and the city core.
setup.intel: Base price $2,620,000, the most expensive base office. Fully upgraded, around $4,860,000 — also the priciest fully kitted out. No targets confirmed from source material yet for this office.

setup.name: Hawick (unconfirmed office)
setup.objective: Listed as a Bail Bonds office in the source material for one target, but this doesn't match the 5 officially purchasable locations (Paleto Bay, Davis, Del Perro, Mission Row, Downtown Vinewood) confirmed elsewhere. Keeping it as its own card rather than dropping the target, but this needs double-checking.

operations.name: Angel Kenney (Lost MC)
operations.objective: Harassment, extortion, theft, and vehicular manslaughter charges, running with a motorcycle gang that terrorizes the neighborhood.
operations.intel: Note: 3 motorcycles are parked at the Cypress Flats location; players pass a 24/7 store en route.
operations.dialogue: Alright, were looking at charges of harassment, extortion, theft, and murder... Among others. That's where Kenney's gang park up. Yep, she's got a fleet of those chopper-lovin' assholes rarin' to go.

required: Bail Office (any one of the five)
recommended: Stun Gun (keeps target alive for full payout)
Personal Quarters upgrade ($295,000, enables fast travel to the office)

notes: Six Most Wanted targets exist in rotation: Grace Whitney, Cleo Song, Brock Thompson, Chaz Lieberman, Leroy O'Neill, and Omar Garcia.

Cleo Song, LJ Ha, and Marquel Green are confirmed targets from the source material but don't have an office stated anywhere in the text, so they're left out of every office card for now rather than guessed at.
Standard bounties can be repeated as many times as wanted; Most Wanted is capped at once per real-world day.

KOR-027.title: The Kortz Center Heist
KOR-027.type: Official GTA Online heist (July 14, 2026 update) requiring a Mansion + Art Studio

overview.target: "La Dernier Debauche" — a newly acquired painting held in the Kortz Center's museum vault, not yet on public display
overview.contact: Mr. Faber (art dealer) via Mr. Deangelis (his fixer/handler), with Rae the forger brought in for the swap
overview.objective: Break into the Kortz Center, swap the real painting with Rae's forgery, wipe the CCTV, and get out clean — so the theft is never even noticed, let alone reported.

KOR-027.intel: Mr. Faber represents a buyer interested in expanding an art collection. He and Deangelis recruit the crew for what Deangelis calls "a classier kind of crime" — no smash and grab, since if the museum notices the painting's gone, Globopol goes after the buyer and the price craters. The plan is a quiet swap: steal the real piece, leave Rae's forgery in its place, erase the security footage, and let nobody be any wiser. Rae, an ULSA art graduate, handles the forgery. Preps are organized under whichever property the crew is currently planning from — Vinewood Mansion, Richman Villa, or Tongva Estate — which changes some mission locations and dialogue but not the overall structure.
KOR-027.dialogue:
Mr Faber: Ahh how wonderful to see you again. We let ourselves in. I'm sure you don't mind. I wanted to see this new art studio of yours... I have a proposition you see. An organization I represent is interested in expanding their collection. They are in need of someone in procurement. Someone hands-on. Someone I believe with your particular qualities.

Mr Deangelis: The organization Faber represents, they want the Kortz Center Collection. Especially their newly acquired Bradeur La Dernier Debauche... This is a classier kind of crime. The Kortz Center. Never been hit before. State of the art tech, secure storage, deadly lasers, your specialty basically. And the painting's not on display yet so we need to access the museum's vault, and this isn't a smash and grab. If they know the painting's gone, you got Globopol on the buyer's ass and you get cents on the dollar.
